title: Router API definition
description: Machine-readable description of one router model's local web API, as observed on one firmware line. A generic client executes a definition; it never contains vendor-specific code.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema the document was written against. Bump only on breaking schema changes.

definitionVersion.description: Semantic version of the definition itself. Patch = clarification, minor = new endpoints/fields, major = removed or renamed ids, changed auth or transport semantics.

vendor.description: Lowercase vendor slug used in paths and in the registry index.

vendorName.description: Vendor name as a person writes it.

model.description: Exact model as the device or the vendor label reports it.

variant.description: Directory name of this variant inside the model directory, e.g. 'v1.0-fw15.03.06.50'.

hardwareVersions.description: Hardware revisions this definition was confirmed on. Empty means the revision was not recorded; it does not mean 'all revisions'.

verified.description: Firmware version string exactly as the device reports it.

match.description: How a client decides this definition applies. 'exact' compares the whole string; 'prefix' compares a dotted-numeric prefix of the version and ignores the locale suffix; 'family' means the vendor published no usable version and the client must use identify probes instead.

matchPrefix.description: For match=prefix: the dotted-numeric prefix to compare, e.g. 'V15.03.06'.

family.description: Firmware family label shared by models that speak the same dialect, e.g. 'goahead-md5-plain'. Definitions in the same family usually need only endpoint-name and field-name corrections.

identify.description: Read-only probes a client runs to confirm this definition matches a live device before it uses any write endpoint.

endpoint.description: Endpoint id from this document used for the probe.

field.description: Dotted path in the probe response holding the model name.

discovery.description: Optional pre-authentication probes a client can run to narrow candidates before spending a login attempt. Every probe must be readable without a session, which is why only plaintext paths appear here.

altHosts.description: Hostnames the vendor answers on besides the IP, e.g. a product domain.

pathPrefix.description: Prefix prepended to every endpoint path. Empty for these devices.

cacheBuster.description: How the device's own UI defeats caching. Purely advisory: the devices ignore the value.

type.description: 'cookie-on-login' means the device sets a session cookie in reply to login; 'http-basic' means every request carries credentials; 'none' means the device has no auth.

cookieName.description: Name of the session cookie when type=cookie-on-login. Leave unset when the device picks its own name.

maxConcurrentSessions.description: Sessions the firmware allows at once. 1 means a second login may evict or be refused by the first, which is the common case on these devices.

body.description: Form body template. Placeholders in the form {password} are replaced by the client using passwordEncoding.

passwordEncoding.description: Transform applied to the plaintext admin password before it is placed in the body. 'md5-hex' is MD5 of the UTF-8 password, lowercase hex.

verified.description: How well this handshake is known. 'not-captured' means the form was never observed on hardware, so a client must refuse to attempt login rather than guess an encoding. Omitting this key means the handshake was captured.

kind.description: 'single' (the default) means one request carries the credentials. 'challenge' means the device first issues a nonce or public key, and the credentials must be encrypted and signed against it -- see the challenge block.

payloadEncoding.description: How the payload values are serialised before encryption. 'form' means application/x-www-form-urlencoded; 'json' means a JSON object.

challenge.description: Present only when kind=challenge. Everything here was read out of the device's own shipped JavaScript, so a client can reproduce the handshake exactly instead of guessing.

issuer.description: The request that hands out the public key and nonce.

extract.description: How to read the key material out of the issuer reply. 'js-vars' means the reply is JavaScript assigning var nn="..."; 'json' means a JSON object. 'map' gives the field name in the reply for each of nn, ee and seq.

hash.description: Digest placed in the signature. 'md5-hex-of-username-plus-password' is MD5(username + password), lowercase hex, with no separator.

cipher.description: Symmetric cipher applied to the payload. The key and IV are generated by the client and sent inside the signature, so the device learns them only by verifying it.

charset.description: Alphabet the random key and IV are drawn from. 'digits' means each character is 0-9, which makes the key 53 bits of entropy per character position rather than a full byte.

keyReport.description: Template by which the client reports its key inside the signature. %key% and %iv% are substituted.

signature.description: How the rendezvous string is signed. The device verifies it with the public half of the key it issued, which is how it recovers the AES key.

plaintext.description: Template for the signed string. %keyReport% is the cipher.keyReport with its substitutions, %hash% is the hash above, %seqPlusDataLen% is the issuer's seq plus the length of the base64 ciphertext.

envelope.description: How sign and data are framed in the request body. %sign% is the RSA signature as hex, %data% is the base64 ciphertext.

payload.description: The plaintext that gets encrypted. JSONDATA prefixes the JSON envelope; the values are the same fields the single-request form would carry.

success.description: How the client must read the reply. 'redirect-to-main' means a 302 whose Location is not the login page. 'body-number' means the body is a bare integer result code. 'cookie-set' means success is a session cookie appearing.

refusalCodes.description: Map of reply code to a stable machine reason the client can localise.

loginPageMarker.description: Substring that proves a reply is the login page rather than an authenticated page.

expiry.description: Signals that the session is gone and the client must log in again.

lockout.description: What the device does after repeated bad passwords. The client must never spend a user's remaining attempts.

crypto.description: Payload protection applied on top of HTTP. Omit entirely when the device sends plain JSON or form data.

iv.description: Initialisation vector as an ASCII string, when the firmware hardcodes it.

perRequest.description: True when the device regenerates the key on every call, so the client must fetch it immediately before each request and must not reuse a cached key.

plaintextPaths.description: Endpoint paths that are never encrypted even though the rest of the API is, e.g. the login form and a native reboot submit.

envelopes.description: How success and failure are expressed across the API, so a client needs no per-endpoint special cases.

resultField.description: Field holding the numeric result code, e.g. 'errCode'.

nonJsonEndpoints.description: Endpoints that answer with a redirect or HTML page instead of a JSON envelope. A client must not parse these as JSON.

verification.description: Weakest link: the level that applies to the least-verified endpoint in this document is recorded per endpoint; this is the overall claim.

capturedOn.description: ISO date of the newest capture behind this document.

unsupported.description: Endpoints whose handler is compiled out on this model. Recorded so a client can explain the gap instead of retrying.

id.description: Stable dotted identifier the client and the capabilities file refer to. Never reuse or rename an id; add a new one and deprecate the old.

path.description: Request path including any fixed query string the firmware requires, e.g. '/goform/cloudv2?module=manage&opt=querybasic'.

uiPage.description: Page of the device's own UI that issues this request, so a maintainer can re-check it by hand.

feature.description: Feature id this endpoint backs, matching a key in the model's capabilities file.

listEncoding.description: How list-valued fields pack rows and columns, for endpoints that replace a whole table in one call.

arrayLayout.description: For json-array replies whose elements are positional rather than uniform.

shapeUnverified.description: True when the endpoint is known to exist but no response was captured. A client may call it but must treat every field as absent.

writes.description: True when the call can change device state.

risk.description: safe = no state change; low = cosmetic or reversible, no client disconnects; medium = disconnects clients or reconfigures one interface; high = drops the WAN or changes working mode; destructive = wipes configuration, flashes firmware, or reboots.

requiresConfirmation.description: The device's own UI gates this behind a confirmation dialog. A client should gate it too.

evidence.description: Where the field list and values came from, short enough to check by hand.

verification.description: live-capture = a raw reply was recorded; live-roundtrip = written and read back unchanged; app-observed = exercised by the Android app against real hardware, raw reply not retained; ui-code = read out of the device's own JavaScript or markup; not-captured = the code path exists but was never exercised; absent = the handler is not compiled into this firmware.

name.description: Wire name exactly as sent or received, including suffixes like '_5g'. Use dotted paths for nested objects.

values.description: The complete accepted value set when the field is an enum. Omit rather than guess.

valueLabels.description: Wire value to the label the vendor's UI shows, when the two differ.

unit.description: Unit and scaling the wire value uses, e.g. 'Mbps x128 -> KB/s'.

secret.description: True when the value is a credential or key that must be redacted before display or logging.
